### Summary
- Clamp CUDA graph free-memory deltas at zero so allocator noise during graph capture cannot produce a negative estimate.
- Apply a final non-negative guard before subtracting the CUDA graph estimate from KV cache allocation.
- Add regression coverage for the estimator and the worker-level available-memory path.

Fixes #44740

### Duplicate check
Before opening this PR:
- `gh issue view 44740 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`: no comments.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "44740 in:body"`: no results.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "negative CUDA graph memory estimation MTP speculative"`: no results.

After opening this PR, those PR searches return only this PR, #44745.

### Tests
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_profile_cudagraph_memory_clamps_free_memory_increases tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_determine_available_memory_clamps_negative_cudagraph_estimate -q`: 2 passed, 17 warnings.
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py`: passed.

### Assistance
AI assistance was used in preparing this change.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for this
  fix! I had opened #45076 for the same issue before finding this PR — closing
  mine in favor of this one. Two small suggestions from my investigation that
  could make this even more robust:

  ### Suggestion 1: Add empty_cache() before each measurement

  The original code calls empty_cache() once before the outer for-mode loop, but
  multiple modes and per-mode captures can accumulate allocator fragmentation
  between measurements. Flushing the caching allocator before each mem_get_info
  snapshot reduces noise:

    for i, desc in enumerate(profile_descs):
        torch.accelerator.empty_cache()  # add this
        mem_before = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0]

  ### Suggestion 2: Emit a warning when negative deltas are detected

  A silent clamp hides a genuine anomaly. If free_after > mem_before, something
  unusual is happening (allocator fragmentation, lazy buffer cleanup, page
  migration). Logging it helps users and maintainers diagnose:

    delta = mem_before - free_after
    if delta < 0:
        logger.warning(
            "CUDA graph capture freed memory (%d MiB); "
            "this may indicate allocator fragmentation or lazy buffer cleanup. "
            "Clamping to zero.",
            -delta // (1 << 20),
        )
    mem_samples.append(max(delta, 0))

  The tests look great — thanks for adding those!
